newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CREYF'S SAYS BOUGHT DUTCH FORESTER.
newsitem.headline: CREYF'S SAYS BOUGHT DUTCH FORESTER.

text.p: Belgian temporary employment company Creyf's NV said in a statement on Tuesday it bought 90 percent of Dutch company Forester BV which in turn owns all of Van den Boom Uitzendbureau and Van den Boom Select.
In the same statement it announced it would increase capital by 400 to 450 million francs by issuing 265,298 new shares respecting the preference rights of existing shareholders.
The issue price of the new shares would be calculated on the basis of the average closing level on the 15 working days leading up to October 9.
The new shares would have the same rights and advantages as the existing shares and would share in profits restrospectively from January 1, 1996.
Ciparco SA, Creyf's controlling shareholder, will exercise its preference rights. The capital increase would be guaranteed by a syndicate lead by Generale Bank .
"Thanks to this new buy in the Netherlands and the capital increase, Creyf's will benefit from the necessary means to develop internal and external expansion," the statement said.
In 1995 employment agency group Van den Boom had turnover of 18.4 million guilders and current profit before tax of 1.17 million guilders.
